title: Thirty-Day Home Health Billing Period Hold under Referrals and Authorizations
content:
Under **Referrals and Authorizations**, a first-period hold protects the provider's thirty-day home health billing period, whose low-utilization threshold turns on the visits made in it, for authorization types that require the patient to be homebound (the Home Health Care Authorization), when the patient confirms the authorization's cancellation.

## Records consulted

- The days passed from the first day of the authorization's validity span to today.
- The servicing provider's lines among the patient's TRICARE Select claim lines dated in the last month.

## Schedule (types that require the patient to be homebound)

| Days passed since the span's first day | Servicing provider's lines dated in the last month | Units held |
|---|---|---|
| fewer than 30 | fewer than 8 | 2 |
| 30 or more | fewer than 8 | 1 |
| any | 8 or more | 0 |

In words: where fewer than thirty days have passed from the first day of the span to today and fewer than eight lines from the servicing provider are dated in the last month, two units are held; where thirty days or more have passed and fewer than eight such lines are dated in the last month, one unit is held; otherwise nothing is held. For a type that does not require the patient to be homebound, nothing is held under this rule.

## Boundary illustrations (hypothetical; span first day 1 April)

| Today | Days passed | Lines in the last month | Units held |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 April | 29 | 5 | 2 |
| 1 May | 30 | 5 | 1 |
| 1 May | 30 | 8 | 0 |
